newsitem.title: USA: Int'l trade to speed move to clean fuels - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Int'l trade to speed move to clean fuels - analyst.

text.p: Expanding international trade may speed the move toward cleaner burning motor fuels for both developed and undeveloped countries alike, a fuel consultant told refining executives Monday.

"While clean fuel regulations, advances in technology and the development of alternative fuels and vehicles have all had an impact on the advance of fuel reformulation, the growing international fuels exchange will accelerate the process," George Unzelman, president of HyOx Inc told executives attending the National Petroleum Refiners Association (NPRA) annual meeting here.

Unzelman said developed and developing countries alike will be spurred on to clean up their fuels, either to get a piece of a growing and lucrative export market, or through imports or refinery upgrades aimed at addressing their own air quality problems.
"Countries in North and South America will look toward the U.S. gasoline and distillate pools as potential markets and will formulate fuel exports accordingly," Unzelman said.
"In the case of Canada and Mexico sophisticated internal reformulation programs are already in place," he said.

He said countries like China, where air pollution problems underscored by rising lung cancer rates are now far ahead of control measures aimed at curtailing the pollution, imports of high quality clean fuels will be a viable solution in the nearer-term.
"Since the area will lag in refining capacity to meet regulatory controls in the foreseeable future, the rapidly expanding fuels exchange network will be the solution," Unzelman said.

Unzelman said California will continue to set the example for global fuel reformulation, though U.S.-wide fuels will likely attain California quality over the longer term, just as fuel specifications outside of the United States look likely to converge in coming years with those of the U.S.
